label: copy phase: current and next output both in {n,h,p,j,f,u,r,1,2}
explanation: 92% of activation mass is in the copy phase, mostly in the middle of the copy (recall_idx 2-5, peak at 3-4). The unit is driven by which tokens are about to be output: out_tok in {n,h,p,j} gives 6-10x lift, and next_out in {h,f,n,p} gives 5-10x lift. It is strongest when both the current and the next output are in this set (e.g. output u/n/h, then h/p). Input tokens t and y raise the rate (3-4x) and appear in most of the top activations, but did not help as standalone predicates. Almost silent at t<2, at the delimiter, and early in the original phase; a small original-phase tail (8% of mass) is not explained. Precision is low (about 0.2): many steps whose outputs are in the set do not fire, so the unit looks like a graded, distributed readout of upcoming-output identity rather than a clean binary feature.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output, by phase (copy phase: n, h, p, j; delimiter step: n, f, j, p; input phase: ) and the next token to output (most: h, f, n, p, r, 2; least: e, q, y, t); timing cues that raise it most: L=4 & t=2, t=3, L=7 & t=5.
